findings.title: English reference lookup is fragile and throws unchecked exception
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file with file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties") and on IOException throws RuntimeException. Any layout that does not match that string rewrite (new theme location, Windows separators, already-English file, missing _en counterpart) aborts verification with an unchecked exception instead of a MojoExecutionException message. The second replaceAll also uses character class [a-zA-Z-_] where the hyphen forms a Z-_ range, so hyphenated locales are not matched as intended.

findings.title: Anchor allow-list mutates a different string than it matched
findings.body: santizeAnchors() iterates Matcher over the original value string but mutates a separate value variable with value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), ""). When the groups are equal it deletes the first occurrence of the English anchor, not the matched occurrence, so reordered or repeated anchors are handled incorrectly. When they differ (e.g. changed href) it adds a message without key/file context, breaks after the first mismatch hiding further anchors, and leaves the offending anchor in place so the same key is reported a second time as Illegal HTML by the caller.

findings.title: Properties read as ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() loads bundles with new PropertyResourceBundle(FileInputStream). That constructor decodes as ISO-8859-1, while the message properties in this repo contain raw UTF-8 (Arabic, Chinese, Thai, etc.). Non-ASCII values are therefore garbled before comparison/sanitizing. The code should load via a Reader with UTF-8, e.g. Files.newBufferedReader(path, UTF_8) plus new PropertyResourceBundle(Reader).
